context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud prior to approval and provides a web interface for fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions. It ensures sub-50ms latency, PCI-DSS compliance, and a 7-year tamper-evident audit trail within AWS `eu-west-1`.

## Key Elements
* **Payment Switch / Core Processing**: External system sending transaction streams and receiving decisions (`approve`, `decline`, `review`).
* **Merchant / Payment Gateway**: External users initiating payment authorizations via API.
* **Fraud Analysts**: Internal users accessing the system via Web UI for case management.
* **Identity Provider (IdP)**: External system providing OAuth2/OIDC authentication for analysts.
* **Model Training Environment (ML Pipeline)**: Decoupled environment pushing updated scoring models via S3.
* **Fraud Screening Core**: Container handling real-time authorization scoring.
* **Case Management Service**: Container managing analyst reviews.
* **Audit & Compliance Archive**: AWS S3 with Object Lock for 7-year tamper-evident storage.

## Relationships
* **Merchant/Payment Gateway to Fraud Screening Core**: REST/gRPC over TLS for authorization requests.
* **Payment Switch to Fraud Screening Core**: gRPC/HTTP over TLS for transaction processing and decision routing.
* **Fraud Analysts to Case Management Service**: HTTPS/TLS for web-based case review.
* **Case Management Service to Identity Provider (IdP)**: OAuth2/OIDC over HTTPS for analyst authentication.
* **Fraud Screening Core to Audit Archive**: AWS SDK/IAM for writing tamper-evident decision logs to AWS S3.
* **ML Pipeline to Fraud Screening Core**: S3 bucket synchronization for zero-downtime model updates.

## Technology Stack
* **Cloud Provider**: AWS (`eu-west-1`) for regional infrastructure and compliance tooling.
* **Communication Protocols**: gRPC and HTTPS over TLS to meet the P99 latency requirement below 50 ms.
* **Storage & Audit**: AWS S3 with Object Lock (Compliance Mode) for low-cost, tamper-evident 7-year audit retention.
* **Authentication**: OAuth2/OIDC for secure analyst access.
* **Model Management**: S3-based artifact distribution for atomic, zero-downtime model updates.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages managed AWS services to maintain PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 7-year tamper-evident audit trail within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Using gRPC and TLS over AWS infrastructure guarantees high throughput and low-latency performance required for real-time fraud screening by a three-engineer team.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations in real-time to detect fraud while enabling analysts to review suspicious transactions. It ensures sub-50ms decision latency and strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance within a fixed AWS budget.

## Key Elements
- **Payment Gateway / External Systems**: Inbound traffic source and core processing systems.
- **Fraud Analysts**: Internal users accessing the case management interface.
- **API Gateway**: AWS API Gateway (REST/HTTP) handling inbound traffic.
- **Scoring Engine**: Go-based microservice deployed on AWS ECS Fargate with an embedded model runtime.
- **Case Management API**: Node.js/Python service on AWS ECS Fargate for fraud analysts.
- **Data Store**: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for transactional data and tamper-evident audit logs.
- **Event Stream**: Amazon SQS for asynchronous event decoupling.

## Relationships
- **Payment Gateway** --(HTTPS/REST)--> **API Gateway**
- **API Gateway** --(gRPC)--> **Scoring Engine**
- **Scoring Engine** --(TCP)--> **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**
- **Scoring Engine** --(AWS SDK/HTTPS)--> **Amazon SQS**
- **Fraud Analysts** --(HTTPS)--> **Case Management API**

## Technology Stack
- **AWS eu-west-1**: Target cloud region for compliance and infrastructure.
- **Go on AWS ECS Fargate**: Selected for the Scoring Engine to achieve <50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS within resource limits.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Chosen for encrypted, append-only tamper-evident audit logging (7-year retention) and PCI-DSS compliance.
- **Amazon SQS**: Utilized for lightweight, low-cost asynchronous event streaming off the critical path.
- **Node.js/Python on AWS ECS Fargate**: Powers the Case Management API for analyst workflows.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages managed AWS services and a streamlined container layout to meet strict performance, security, and auditability requirements without exceeding the 25,000 EUR monthly budget or overwhelming a 3-engineer team. Asynchronous decoupling via SQS ensures critical real-time payment paths easily maintain sub-50ms latencies.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations within 50 ms to prevent fraud while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. It enables fraud analysts to review flagged transactions and supports zero-downtime model updates within AWS.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / External Systems
- Fraud Analysts
- API Gateway (AWS API Gateway HTTP API with Rust/Go Lambda Authorizer)
- Scoring Engine (Go, AWS ECS Fargate, Embedded Model Runtime)
- Case Management API (Node.js/Python, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Data Store (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL)
- Event Stream (Amazon SQS)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> API Gateway: Sends payment authorizations [HTTPS/REST]
- API Gateway -> Scoring Engine: Dispatches scoring requests [gRPC over VPC Link]
- Scoring Engine -> Data Store: Persists audit logs and decisions [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol / TLS]
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management API: Reviews suspicious payments [HTTPS/REST]

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway: Provides low-latency edge routing and rate limiting.
- Go (AWS ECS Fargate): Powers the Scoring Engine for high throughput and sub-50ms latency.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Stores audit logs and case data with 7-year retention.
- Amazon SQS: Handles asynchronous event streaming for case management updates.

## Rationale
The serverless edge and containerized Go architecture guarantees sub-50ms P99 latency under heavy throughput. Strict tokenization and Aurora PostgreSQL audit logging satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year tamper-evident compliance requirements within budget.

Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud within strict performance and compliance constraints. It provides real-time scoring, case management for analysts, and tamper-evident audit logging on AWS.

## Key Elements
- **API Handler (`Go`)**: Manages inbound gRPC requests from the API Gateway.
- **Token Sanitizer (`Go`)**: Redacts and tokenizes raw Primary Account Numbers (PAN).
- **Rule Engine (`Go`)**: Evaluates deterministic business rules in-memory.
- **Model Runner (`Go` + ONNX Runtime)**: Executes compiled machine learning models locally.
- **Audit Logger (`Go`)**: Asynchronously generates and persists tamper-evident decision logs.
- **Data Store (`Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL`)**: Stores transactional data and audit logs.

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> API Handler: Routes authorization requests via gRPC.
- API Handler -> Token Sanitizer: Passes raw requests via synchronous in-process calls.
- Token Sanitizer -> Rule Engine & Model Runner: Forwards sanitized feature vectors via synchronous in-process calls.
- Rule Engine & Model Runner -> Audit Logger: Dispatches event data via Go channels.
- Audit Logger -> Data Store: Writes audit logs via TCP.

## Technology Stack
- **Go**: Chosen for high concurrency and low memory footprint to meet P99 < 50ms latency at 3,000 RPS.
- **ONNX Runtime**: Enables low-latency in-process machine learning model execution without network hops.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Provides reliable, ACID-compliant storage for transactions and 7-year audit requirements.
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Minimizes operational overhead for a 3-engineer team within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Rationale
This architecture achieves sub-50ms latency and high availability by executing scoring logic in-process without network overhead. It strictly enforces PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year auditability while remaining maintainable for a three-engineer team.

Case Management API.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management API is a container component powering fraud analyst review workflows and tamper-evident audit logging for the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system. It securely manages suspicious payment cases while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts: External users reviewing suspicious payment cases via web UI.
- Case Controller: Node.js/Express service exposing REST endpoints for analyst workflows.
- Audit & Evidence Service: Component capturing analyst decisions with cryptographically verifiable hashes.
- Case Repository: Data access layer interacting with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.
- Masking & Tokenization Proxy: Interceptor middleware ensuring card numbers are redacted.

## Relationships
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Controller [HTTPS/JSON]
- Case Controller -> Audit & Evidence Service [In-process Function Call]
- Case Controller -> Case Repository [TCP/PostgreSQL Protocol]
- Case Repository -> Masking & Tokenization Proxy [In-process Middleware]

## Technology Stack
- TypeScript / Node.js with Express: Provides rapid development velocity suited for a three-engineer team.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Shared persistent data store for relational case data.
- Prisma / Axios Interceptors: Implements consistent data masking and redaction at the application boundary.

## Rationale
This component architecture fits requirements by isolating security-sensitive workflows, ensuring analysts never see unmasked card data, and generating tamper-evident audit trails within a constrained team size and budget.

Data Store.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations in real time and provides a case management interface for fraud analysts. It runs on AWS in the `eu-west-1` region to meet stringent PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability requirements.

## Key Elements
- **Payment Switch / Core Processing & Merchant Gateway**: External systems initiating authorization requests.
- **Fraud Analysts**: Human users reviewing suspicious payments via case management.
- **API Gateway**: AWS API Gateway (REST/HTTP) ingress point.
- **Scoring Engine**: Go application hosted on AWS ECS Fargate with an embedded model runtime.
- **Case Management API**: Node.js/Python application on AWS ECS Fargate for analyst workflows.
- **Data Store (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL)**: Composed of Transactional Database, Audit Ledger, Model & Feature Store Schema, and Connection Pooler (PgBouncer/Aurora Proxy).
- **Event Stream**: Amazon SQS.

## Relationships
- **Merchant Gateway -> API Gateway**: Submits payment authorizations via HTTPS/REST.
- **API Gateway -> Scoring Engine**: Forwards authorization payloads via gRPC/HTTP2.
- **Scoring Engine -> Connection Pooler**: Writes decisions and audit logs via TCP (PostgreSQL Wire Protocol).
- **Case Management API -> Connection Pooler**: Manages review cases via TCP (PostgreSQL Wire Protocol).
- **Scoring Engine -> Event Stream**: Publishes asynchronous audit events via AWS SDK/SQS.

## Technology Stack
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Minimizes operational overhead for the 3-engineer team.
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Unifies transactional data, audit logs, and feature storage within budget.
- **PgBouncer / Aurora Proxy**: Prevents connection exhaustion under 3,000 TPS load.
- **Go**: Ensures P99 decision latency below 50 ms.

## Rationale
This architecture uses managed AWS services to remain within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget while supporting a 3-engineer team. Cryptographic hash-chaining in PostgreSQL satisfies 7-year tamper-evident auditability without specialized ledger costs.

Event Stream.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect and review fraud prior to approval. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS, and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a fixed 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts (Users)
- Payment Switch / Core Processing, Merchant / Payment Gateway, Identity Provider (IdP), Model Training Environment (External Systems)
- API Gateway (AWS API Gateway)
- Scoring Engine (Go, AWS ECS Fargate, Embedded Model Runtime)
- Case Management API (Node.js / Python, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Data Store (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL)
- Event Stream (Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with Kinesis Data Firehose)
- Long-Term Audit Storage (Amazon S3)

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway -> API Gateway: Submits payment authorization requests [HTTPS / REST]
- API Gateway -> Scoring Engine: Forwards authorization requests for real-time scoring [gRPC / Internal VPC]
- Scoring Engine -> Data Store: Reads rules/models and writes transaction logs [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol / TCP]
- Scoring Engine -> Event Stream: Publishes asynchronous decision events [AWS Kinesis SDK / HTTPS]
- Event Stream -> Amazon S3: Streams decision data via Kinesis Data Firehose for audit logging [AWS Internal HTTPS / IAM]
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management API: Reviews suspicious payments and manages cases [HTTPS / REST]
- Case Management API -> Data Store: Reads and updates case data [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol / TCP]

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Target cloud provider ensuring managed scalability within budget constraints
- Go: Used for the Scoring Engine to achieve low sub-50ms P99 latency at high throughput
- Node.js / Python: Used for the Case Management API to enable rapid feature delivery by a 3-engineer team
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Provides ACID compliance for relational case management and transaction data
- Amazon Kinesis Data Streams & Firehose: Provides partitioned event streaming and log replay capabilities for auditability and model updates

## Rationale
The architecture combines Go-based microservices on AWS ECS Fargate with Kinesis streaming to process 3,000 TPS under 50ms while maintaining strict audit trails. Serverless and managed AWS services minimize operational overhead, allowing a three-engineer team to operate the system securely and reliably within the 25,000 EUR budget.
